harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented, via an Ansible playbook run from the control node (node4), a router topology where node1 bridges two private networks (lan-a to node2, lan-b to node3). node2's egress toward node3 is capped at 1 Mbit/s with a tc tbf qdisc applied automatically on interface bring-up; node3's egress toward node2 is left unrestricted. All four nodes were individually restarted and verified to recover with persisted configuration.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: mgmt network (eth0, all 4 nodes) plus previously-unconfigured lan-a (node1 eth1 <-> node2 eth1) and lan-b (node1 eth2 <-> node3 eth1)

Set up passwordless SSH from control node node4 to node1 (vyos user), node2, node3 (root); discovered and fixed locked root accounts (which blocked pubkey auth) by generating random passwords on the nodes themselves
Installed python3 (Ansible requirement) and iproute2-tc on node2/node3 via apk

Wrote and ran an Ansible playbook (/root/ts-ansible/playbook.yml on node4) that configures VyOS eth1/eth2 addresses on node1 via a templated configure/commit/save script, writes /etc/network/interfaces on node2 with a static eth1 address, a route to node3's subnet, and a tc tbf qdisc (1mbit) applied via an 'up' hook, and writes /etc/network/interfaces on node3 with a static eth1 address and route only (no shaping)
Verified with iperf3: node2->node3 throughput ~1.0-1.5 Mbit/s (capped), node3->node2 throughput ~1 Gbit/s (unrestricted)

Captured pre-restart boot IDs and health evidence for all 4 nodes, restarted each node one at a time via native reboot, polled until reachable, and verified changed boot IDs plus full recovery of interfaces, routes, tc qdisc, and end-to-end connectivity/throughput

Discovered VyOS regenerates authorized_keys from committed config at boot (wiping the manually-added key); fixed by committing the SSH public key into VyOS's own config via 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys' so Ansible access and playbook idempotency survive future reboots
Re-ran the Ansible playbook after all restarts to confirm fully idempotent, error-free reconciliation across all three managed nodes

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 sit on separate private networks and communicate through node1
evidence.summary: Confirmed node1 has eth1 (lan-a, toward node2) and eth2 (lan-b, toward node3) previously unconfigured; assigned 10.10.12.1/24 and 10.10.13.1/24 on node1, 10.10.12.2/24 on node2, 10.10.13.2/24 on node3; ping from node2 to node3's private IP and vice versa succeeds only via node1 forwarding (ip_forward=1, no direct L2 path).

evidence.requirement: Limit traffic from node2 toward node3 to 1 Mbit/s
evidence.summary: tc qdisc tbf rate 1Mbit applied on node2 eth1 (the only path to node3); iperf3 node2->node3 throughput measured at ~1.0-1.5 Mbit/s both before and after the reboot cycle.

evidence.requirement: Leave traffic from node3 toward node2 unrestricted
evidence.summary: node3 eth1 has default pfifo_fast qdisc (no shaping); iperf3 node3->node2 throughput measured at ~1 Gbit/s.

Playbook /root/ts-ansible/playbook.yml run via ansible-playbook from control node node4 (as designated in environment.toml) configures node1 (vyos), node2, and node3; second run post-reboot is fully idempotent (no unexpected changes, no failures).

Baseline boot_id ebd78841...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to 83832900...; interfaces, ip_forward, vyos-router service, and cross-network pings all recovered.

Baseline boot_id 7301a9a7...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to 7d543419...; eth1 address, route to node3, and tc tbf qdisc (1mbit) all recovered automatically via ifupdown-ng 'up' hooks; ping to node3 succeeded.

Baseline boot_id a18fee07...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to a65d3d6f...; eth1 address and route to node2 recovered, no shaping qdisc present (as required); ping to node2 succeeded.

Baseline boot_id adba3716...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to 422401bf... with uptime -s matching the reboot time; recovery proven by successfully re-running the Ansible playbook against all managed nodes afterward.
